title: runtime-length-gauge-prefill-priority-condenser
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Introduce a runtime "length gauge" and a lightweight "batch condenser" that cooperates with prefill/decode schedulers and kernel selection to reduce wasted token padding across bursty traffic. The approach focuses on soft-trimming long tail sequences, probabilistic slot consolidation for short sequences, and generating kernel affinity hints to favor attention kernels that benefit from denser batches. Goal: reduce median token-cost-per-request by ~12-18% on mixed workloads while keeping p95 latency within SLO.
acceptance_criteria: Length gauge emits per-shard histogram of active token spans (1-8, 9-32, 33-128, 129+) on each 10s window.
Batch condenser groups pending requests by gauge bucket and soft-trim policy with <1ms additional scheduling overhead.
Kernel hinting API returns preferred kernel variant and estimated throughput delta for each condensed batch.
End-to-end integration reduces padded tokens per batch by >=12% on internal mixed-text benchmark (chat + long-form generation).
No regression in p95 latency beyond configured SLO (runtime-1.24 target: p95 increase <= 5%).
Unit and e2e tests covering gauge emission, condensation decisions, and kernel hint fallbacks are merged.
implementation_notes: Length gauge: lightweight sampling on request enqueue and after prefill to avoid double counting; maintain sliding histograms per worker and aggregate via leader every 10s.

Condenser: soft-trim trims trailing tokens probabilistically (alpha tunable) instead of hard truncation to preserve quality; short sequences may be concatenated into a single slot with per-request offsets preserved via KV slot maps.

Kernel hinting: map gauge buckets to candidate kernels (dense-attn, sparse-attn, tiled-matmul). Use microbenchmarks to estimate delta; provide hint object (kernel_name, expected_tokens_per_ms, fallback_ok).
Scheduler integration: condenser is invoked pre-prefill for batches older than X ms and pre-decode for cadence-driven batches; exposes telemetry for decisions to Console.
Fallbacks: if condenser causes quality regression above threshold in A/B test, automatically disable for that customer and log to rollout dashboard.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive trimming reduces cost but can degrade generation quality on long-tail prompts; we mitigate with probabilistic soft-trim and per-prompt heuristics.
Concatenating short sequences increases effective batch density but requires careful KV-offset management and memory accounting; risk of higher memory pressure on peak.
Kernel hinting adds complexity to scheduler heuristics; inaccurate hints can cause suboptimal kernel choices—hence we keep fallback_ok and conservative defaults.
test_plan: Microbench: run synthetic traffic with controlled seqlen distribution to validate padded-token reduction and kernel throughput estimates.
Integration: end-to-end test in staging across hosted and dedicated pools, measuring token-cost, median/p95 latency, and generation fidelity on a held-out eval set.
Canary: rollout to 5% traffic with automatic rollback if per-customer quality alerts or latency SLO breaches occur.
Regression: nightly job comparing runtime-1.24 baseline metrics against changes, trigger alerts on >5% cost reduction accompanied by >3% quality drop.
